reason: The code and the schedule are feasible. The pre-registered gate is not, so the chance of a scored probe is about 0.05-0.1, far below 0.7. (1) Numbers checked: the cited logs match (leak5 OOF public 1.5254 / P 1.2375 / Q 1.4278; kill test P +11.99/+0.19 %, Q +6.31/+1.32 %; P all-peak z shift +0.567 vs public -0.021). (2) The idea's premise does not hold on 44b6. I pooled the per-embryo leak5 OOF from out_full_{P,Q}/report.json (folds[*].eval.per_embryo). On 44b6, Q is +3.9 % WORSE than the public head (1.3468 vs 1.2963 um) and P is +3.6 % worse, even though Q saw the other 44b6 folds. After dropping the probable x138 training videos, both heads are out-of-sample on the same clips, and Q is still +3.1 % worse (1.3413 vs 1.3006); Q beats public on only 20/71 44b6 videos. Q's pooled -6.4 % comes entirely from 6bba (-7.9 %), which holds 85 % of the pairs. So the 'asymmetric test' does not explain the FAIL: the public head wins on 44b6 at equal exposure. (3) By convexity of the distance, the blend is at most the average of its two members. For gate (b), on 44b6 that bound is +1.6..2.0 % vs public, but the gate requires <= -5 %, so the blend would have to beat the average of its members by about 6.5 %. These are two heads on the same 224-d features with the same targets, so their errors are highly correlated; P(pass) is below 0.1 (a guess). Gate (a), 6bba->44b6: the bound is +3.15 % and the gate needs <= 0 %, so it needs a >= 3.2 % ensemble gain; P about 0.25. Gates (c) (Q's y gap 0.21 -> about 0.11 < 0.15) and (d) (Q m7 >= public in both embryo folds) probably pass. Joint P(gate pass) is about 0.05-0.1, not 0.35. (4) Resource error in the idea: a kernel run on kaggle-sasyami cannot be submitted by vitaliineibauer. The dummy run must be a completed version on the submitting account, so it waits for the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC quota reset (fine for the timeline). (5) Schedule given a gate pass is about 0.9 (below). By the idea's own rule a failed gate cannot be loosened, so P(scored LB probe) = P(gate) x 0.9 is about 0.05-0.09.
fix_if_any: Nothing honest raises the chance of a scored probe to 0.7. Relaxing gate (b) on 44b6 to 'no worse' would make it passable, but the best case on 44b6-like data then tends to 0 (-0.0005..0 LB), and that is exactly the kind of loosening the idea forbids. Cheapest honest version: spend at most 1 h of agent time adding a Blend method to tools/train_coordhead.py (evaluate() already builds methods=[NoShift, public, new, Ridge]; add BlendShift(public, new, W) in um before the 2 um bound, and report it in the leak5 per-embryo and embryo-held-out tables for W in {0.25, 0.5}). The user runs it once on the PC that holds the captures (about 5 min CPU, --debias embryo --huber-delta 0.5 --epochs 120, as in out_full_Q). Pre-register this prediction: FAIL at (b) on 44b6. Build the kernel patch (--base x138 --patch headblend, a second head via V1284_HEAD2, V1284_BLEND_W=0 must be byte-identical to exp56) only if (a)-(d) pass as written. If the table shows the blend <= 0.97x public on 44b6 at leak5, it is worth a look; otherwise close the line for good.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 expected (the most likely outcome is that the gate fails and nothing is submitted). If it were forced onto the LB: -0.001 to +0.001, below the ~0.003 LB noise. On 44b6-like data the blend is bounded at +1.6..2 % worse distance than public.
realistic_private_gain: ~0 expected; if forced, -0.0015 to +0.001. Private embryos are unseen; Q's only gain is within 6bba, and on the other train embryo Q loses to public even at equal exposure, so the gain does not generalise across embryos.

Friend A is not needed. 17:00-20:00 UTC: #34/#35 score and decide the base (x138 if #34 = 0.953, else exp51 via the exp55 COORDHEAD_HEAD_PATH route). IF the gate passes: 20:00-22:00 UTC, the user uploads the private 33 KB dataset of the Q head (kaggle datasets create). The agent adds a 'headblend' patch to tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 (currently only divinsert|leafprune are allowed), editing x138's module string to load a second head plus V1284_BLEND_W, with a byte-identical check at W=0; about 1.5-2 h. 26 Sep 00:00 UTC: vitaliineibauer quota resets. 00:05-01:00 UTC: push and dummy run on vitaliineibauer, about 30 min GPU (exp51 took 1,713 s). This must be the submitting account, not sasyami. If the user is asleep and has not pre-approved, this slips to 07:00 UTC. 26 Sep 07:00-08:00 UTC: submit after the user's OK, 1 of 5 slots on 26 Sep. Scored about 14:00-18:00 UTC 26 Sep, well within the x138 12 h limit (the second MLP adds negligible runtime). About 2.7 days of slack before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC, so P(scored | gate pass) is about 0.9. The binding constraint is the gate: P(pass) about 0.05-0.1, so P(scored) is about 0.05-0.09.
